Hi all — tax perspective below. We should treat both invoices as UK VAT-taxable and split VAT proportionally by net amounts. Example calculation based on Sarah’s requested allocation:

- Net: INV-7601 = GBP 90,000; INV-7602 = GBP 60,000
- VAT @20%: INV-7601 VAT = 18,000; INV-7602 VAT = 12,000
- Total matches paid VAT on the receipt (assuming payment included VAT).

Recommended postings:
- Use tax code VAT-SPLIT-2026Q2 for the adjustment entries so they’re easy to query during audit.
- Update reclaim/return schedule to reflect the split if Helix reclaims VAT.
- If any FX revaluation is required (payment cleared in GBP), we will account for immaterial FX rounding in the suspense account; agree with Grace’s JV approach.

I’ve attached a short note with the calculation and suggested ledger mapping (tax_note_vat_split.docx).
